_readme: Single source of truth for the India Datathon website. Edit this file, then run: python3 build.py

site._preview: true = shows the 'Design preview' bar and tells search engines not to index. Set false only when the organizer has approved the public copy.
site._urlPending: When the domain owner has pointed indiadatathon.org at GitHub Pages: set url back to https://indiadatathon.org/, restore the CNAME file (one line: indiadatathon.org), rebuild and push.
site.credit: Website designed and managed by Pulkit Chatwal
site._url: Final public address, e.g. https://indiadatathon.org/ (used for share previews). Leave empty until the domain is confirmed.

event.name: India Datathon
event.tagline: Clinical questions. Shared expertise. Hands-on health data science.
event.intro: Two days for medical and data science/engineering participants to work together on clinical questions using a large hospital dataset and an AWS-based platform.
event._hostLogo: Official Apollo Hospitals logo files, unmodified, from apollohospitals.com. Leave both empty to show the host name as text instead.
event._mapEmbedUrl: The live Google Map shown in the Venue section. Leave empty to show the India Gate drawing instead.

registration._state: upcoming | open | waitlist | closed.  An FAQ item may carry q_open / a_open / a_closed etc. to change its wording with the state.
registration.opensText: Registration opens in the second half of December 2026.
registration._formEmbed: true = when registration is open, the Google Form is shown inside the page (with a button to open it in its own tab). false = button only. Needs the long docs.google.com/forms/d/e/…/viewform link, not a forms.gle short link.
registration._formUrl: The Google Form link printed by google-form/create-form.gs ('Share this link'). Paste it here, then set state to open on opening day. Until state is open the page keeps showing the locked preview.
registration._formEndpoint: Or: an address that accepts the built-in form as a POST (Formspree, Google Apps Script, your own API). With state open and this set, the built-in form becomes live.

signup._mode: off | demo | live.  off = no email form at all (the safe fallback).  demo = form is shown for design review and saves NOTHING.  live = posts the email to 'endpoint'.
signup._successState: pending = service uses double opt-in ('check your email').  confirmed = address is subscribed immediately.

contacts._note: Leave empty until approved. Empty contacts are never shown as broken buttons.

faculty.name: Leo Anthony Celi
faculty.bio: Leo Anthony Celi directs MIT Critical Data. His work brings clinicians and data scientists together to study routinely collected health data and improve the way clinical evidence is developed.

faculty.name: Anirban Bhattacharyya
faculty.bio: Anirban Bhattacharyya is a critical care specialist at Mayo Clinic in Florida. His interests include the development and application of artificial intelligence in intensive care and mentoring trainees in clinical research.

faculty.name: Sujoy Kar
faculty.bio: Sujoy Kar is Chief Medical Information Officer at Apollo Hospitals. His work includes clinical artificial intelligence, digital health and the adoption of data-informed approaches in health care.

faculty.name: Piyush Mathur
faculty.bio: Piyush Mathur is an anesthesiologist and intensivist at Cleveland Clinic and a founder of BrainX. His work spans clinical care, quality improvement and applications of artificial intelligence in health care.

faculty.name: Sulagna Bhattacharjee
faculty.bio: Sulagna Bhattacharjee is a faculty member in anaesthesiology, pain medicine and critical care at AIIMS, New Delhi.

faculty.name: Anirban Hom Choudhuri
faculty.bio: Anirban Hom Choudhuri is Director Professor and Head of Critical Care Medicine at Vardhman Mahavir Medical College & Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi. His research examines septic shock, ICU-acquired infections and outcomes in critically ill patients, including studies using routinely collected clinical data. His published work also addresses antimicrobial resistance and end-of-life care in the ICU.

faculty.name: Terri L. Menser
faculty.bio: Terri L. Menser is a health services researcher at Mayo Clinic. She studies practice improvement, patient outcomes, health disparities and the implementation of interventions and health information technology.

faculty.name: Tavpritesh Sethi
faculty.bio: Tavpritesh Sethi is Professor of Computational Biology and founding head of the Center of Excellence in Healthcare at IIIT-Delhi. His work connects medicine and computation, including clinical decision support and machine learning for critical care and community health.

faculty.name: Mayank Garg
faculty.bio: Mayank Garg is a physician-scientist and Simons-Ashoka Early Career Fellow at Ashoka University. His work connects clinical questions, experimental research and health data science.

faculty.name: Swapnil Mishra
faculty.bio: Swapnil Mishra is an Assistant Professor at the NUS Saw Swee Hock School of Public Health, with a joint appointment at the NUS Institute of Data Science. His research combines global health, machine learning and Bayesian modelling.

faculty.name: Vinayak Mathur
faculty.affiliation: Dure Technologies / Terablu Climate Technologies / Eldric Group
faculty.bio: Vinayak Mathur is Envoy, Special Projects at Dure Technologies and a board member of Terablu Climate Technologies and Eldric Group.

faculty.name: Amit Agarwal
faculty.bio: Amit Agarwal is a Research Manager at Capital One, where he works on AI safety.

faculty.name: Pushkar Shukla
faculty.bio: Pushkar Shukla works on AI safety at Cloudphysician.AI. His research interests include fairness, computer vision and interpretability, with work on bias detection and mitigation, counterfactual causal analysis and safety evaluations.

faculty.name: Mengling (Mornin) Feng
faculty.bio: Mengling (Mornin) Feng is an Associate Professor at the NUS Saw Swee Hock School of Public Health, with appointments in Biomedical Engineering and the Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine at the National University of Singapore. He leads Group Mornin for Healthcare AI, and his work focuses on machine learning and artificial intelligence for health care.

items.q: When and where is India Datathon?
items.a: 24–25 January 2027, at Indraprastha Apollo Hospitals in New Delhi. The event is in person only. Both days finish at 6:00 PM IST.

A short, collaborative event where people with different expertise investigate questions using a shared dataset. At India Datathon, clinical and technical participants work together to frame a useful clinical question, examine the data and explain what their findings can support.
Approximately 80, with an even split between medical and data science/engineering backgrounds.

items.q: What dataset and platform will we use?
items.a: A large hospital dataset and an AWS-based platform. The specific dataset is to be announced. Access requirements and preparation instructions will follow.

items.q: Which clinical tracks can I work on?
items.a: Specific clinical tracks are to be announced. Questions will follow the five guardrails in About.
Registration opens in the second half of December 2026. Join the email notification list to hear when it opens. Joining the list does not reserve a place.
items.a_nosignup: Registration opens in the second half of December 2026. The exact date will be announced on this page.
items.a_open: Registration is open. Fill in the participation form on this site. Apply individually; submitting the form does not by itself confirm a place.

items.q: Who can apply? Do I need to code?
items.a: Students and professionals from medical and data science/engineering backgrounds can apply. Medical participants do not need to code. Technical participants should know Python (preferred), R or SQL. Bring curiosity and a willingness to work with and learn from teammates with different expertise.

items.q: Can I apply individually? How are teams formed?
items.a: Yes, apply as an individual. Organizers will form teams with a balanced mix of clinical knowledge and technical skills.
The fee amount is to be announced.

items.q: Are meals, travel and accommodation provided?
items.a: Meals will be provided. Participants are responsible for their own travel and accommodation.

Each team will give a five-minute presentation about what it built. Tell the story behind the work: the clinical question, what the data could support, the decisions, disagreements and changes along the way, and how clinical and technical perspectives shaped your approach. The journey and reasoning matter more than a polished end product.

items.q: Will there be certificates and prizes?
items.a: Participants will receive certificates. Prizes will be awarded to the top three teams; prize details will be announced.

Yes. Generative AI use is encouraged. The LLMathon will help teams compare AI responses, question their reliability and decide what counts as evidence. Teams remain responsible for the reasoning behind their work.

items.q: Who owns the code? What happens after the event?
items.a: Teams own the code they create. Any publication or continued data access after the event must be arranged separately by the participants involved.

form._note: The participation form. Questions follow the ESICM Datathon 2027 registration form, adapted for India Datathon (no language question, 'Medical care experience' instead of intensive care, no Milan presentation question). Shown locked ('Coming soon') while registration.state is 'upcoming'. Every build also writes google-form/create-form.gs, which creates the same questions as a Google Form. Field types: text, email, tel, textarea, select, radio, checks, confirm.
